Drawing rangoli this season? Go down on one knee instead of bending from the waist.

Bent over, the lower back holds you up for the whole design. Down on one knee, on a folded mat or towel, the legs share the work. Switch knees every few minutes and stand for a stretch between borders.

Save this post for the festive weeks ahead.

#wellnessathome #familycare #indianparents #jointcare

Practise copying from across the room, not just from the page.

Much of the writing at school is copied from a board. At home, stick one word on the fridge and let your child copy it at the table: look up, hold the word in mind, write it down. It builds the same habit, gently.

What word would you put on your fridge first? Tell us below.

#handwritingpractice #studyathome #kidslearning #indianparents

Every small letter lives on one of three floors: tall, middle or hanging.

Tall letters like b, d and h reach the top line. Middle letters like a, c and e stay between the base line and the dotted line. Hanging letters like g, p and y drop their tails below. Teach the floor, and the size of each letter looks after itself.

Swipe through, then save this post for the next practice page.

#handwritingpractice #kidslearning #studyathome #shribazaar

Slow circles around the kneecap, not on it.

Scoop a little of our Instant Pain Relief Soothing Massage Gel onto the fingertips and work it in with slow circles around the edge of the kneecap, then long strokes above and below the knee. It's cooling, fast-absorbing and dries without leaving the skin sticky. Pack of 2 jars, for external use only.

Link in bio to see the gel.

#jointcare #kneepain #shribazaar #madeforindia

Did your school pick the neatest handwriting in the class?

Some schools held a yearly competition, some pinned the best page on the notice board, and some teachers simply read out a name on Friday. Almost everyone remembers who it was.

What did your school do? Tell us in the comments.

#handwritingpractice #indianparents #familycare

Lift the little one with your legs, not your back.

Small children get picked up from the floor many times a day. Feet apart with one slightly ahead, bend the knees and keep the back tall, then bring the child in close before you stand.

A small habit for parents and grandparents alike.

#familycare #wellnessathome #jointcare #indianparents

Close your eyes and trace it.

The letters in our Magic Practice Copybook are pressed into the page as grooves, so a child can feel them as well as see them. Once a letter is familiar, try it with eyes closed and let the fingertip find the path. The set has four books, one pen and ten refills, and the ink fades so pages can be practised again.

It's a practice aid for children aged 3 and up. Link in bio.

#kidslearning #handwritingpractice #madeforindia #shribazaar

A long journey home for the festival? Make it kinder on the knees and back.

Lift a heavy bag in two moves, seat first and rack second. Circle the ankles every hour. Tuck a rolled shawl behind the waist. And stand up to walk a few steps at every long halt.

Save this post before you pack.

#wellnessathome #jointcare #familycare #dailyuse

You say it, they write it: hand the grocery list to your child.

Real words with a real job make practice feel useful. Atta, dal, milk, tomatoes: every item is a small spelling lesson, and the list really goes to the shop with you.

Try it before the next market run.

#kidslearning #studyathome #familycare #dailyuse

The end of a walk should be the slowest part.

Instead of stopping at full pace, ease off for the last few minutes. Then, at the gate, rest one hand on the wall and give each calf a gentle stretch before you go inside.

Who keeps the evening walk going in your family?

#wellnessathome #jointcare #indianparents

Which seat is the hardest to get up from: the soft sofa, the floor or the plastic chair?

A sofa sinks low and gives little to push against. The floor asks the most of the knees. A light plastic chair can slide back just as you rise. Every home has one seat everyone avoids.

Tell us A, B or C in the comments.

#jointcare #kneepain #familycare #shribazaar

Give every stroke a word, and new letters get easier to remember.

For b: top of the line, big line down, then up and round the tummy. Saying the path out loud while the pen moves gives a child something to hold on to when a letter is new.

Which letter needs its own little rhyme at your home?

#handwritingpractice #kidslearning #indianparents

At the sink, rest one foot inside the cabinet.

Open the door below the sink and rest one foot on the ledge while you wash up, swapping feet every few minutes. It's a small change that stops the lower back from carrying all of the standing.

Save this post for the next big pile of dishes.

#wellnessathome #dailyuse #jointcare #familycare

Keep the practice books on a low shelf.

When a child can reach the books and the pen without asking, practice starts more often on its own. One spot, everything together, at their height.

Where do the study books live at your home?

#studyathome #kidslearning #shribazaar #madeforindia

Cooler nights? Keep the knees covered.

As the evenings turn cool, a light shawl over the knees while watching TV and a blanket that reaches the feet at night can make mornings feel easier.

Good night from all of us at Shri Bazaar.

#familycare #jointcare #indianparents #wellnessathome

Weeds never come up evenly across a bed. They hide in four spots.

Seen from above, a kitchen-garden bed fills up in the same places every season: right at the base of a plant stem, along the edge beside the path, where water collects under the drip line, and beside the stakes and supports you tie plants to. Knowing your spot tells you where to weed first.

खरपतवार क्यारी में कहाँ छिपते हैं?

Which spot fills up first in your bed: 1, 2, 3 or 4? Tell us in the comments.

#बागवानी #kitchengarden #weeding #bagiya

No spray, no mixing: dry granules go straight from the pack.

BAGIYA Weed Killer Granules are for ground you want completely clear: wall bases, paths, drain edges and plot corners. Sprinkle onto the soil at the base, water lightly, and leave it to work at the root. No tank to fill and nothing to dilute.

స్ప్రే లేదు. కలపడం లేదు.

They clear whatever they reach, so never use them on lawns, beds or crops you are keeping. Wear gloves; keep away from children, pets and plants you want. Link in bio.

Wall, path, drain, corner: four places, four ways to keep them clear.

The ground around a house fills up in the same four places. Wall base: keep a strip about a step wide clear and seal cracks in the plinth. Paths: sweep the joints while dry and fill wide gaps. Drain edge: lift the silt out after rain and keep the lip clear. Plot corner: clear it before it flowers, because a corner in seed seeds the whole plot.

சுவர், பாதை, வடிகால், மூலை: நான்கு இடங்கள், நான்கு வழிகள்.

Ground you want completely clear is a job for granules; beds you are keeping are a job for a hand tool. Save this post for the next clean-up. Which of the four takes most of your time?

#களை #tamilnadu #gardeningindia #bagiya

Clean the drain, and the weeds on its lip still come back first.

Here is an open drain cut in half. Water seeps through a joint in the wall into the bank beside it, and the roots of the weeds on the lip grow toward that damp seam. Scraping the channel clean does nothing to them. The root zone on the outer bank is where granules act, never in the water itself.

ഓട വൃത്തിയാക്കിയാലും, അരികിലെ കള ആദ്യം തിരിച്ചുവരും.

Which is the drain by your house: 1 open concrete, 2 unlined earth channel, or 3 covered with slabs?

#കള #kerala #weedcontrol #growandguard

Made for the gaps between rows: 20 cm across, five pointed teeth.

The BAGIYA 5-Teeth Weeding Rake Head, measured: 20 cm across, 14 cm teeth and a 3.2 cm socket, with five pointed carbon-steel teeth. Narrow enough to work between rows of plants you are keeping, and it loosens the soil as it lifts the weed.

कतारों के बीच के लिए बना।

Sow the next rows a little wider than your tool. 🌱

When rows sit too close, no tool fits between them and every weed becomes a hand job. Leave the gap between the leaves of neighbouring rows a bit wider than a 20 cm rake head, and a single stroke can run the length of the bed without touching a plant.

अगली बुवाई में कतारें थोड़ी चौड़ी रखिए।

How far apart are the rows in your bed right now?

#kitchengarden #terracegarden #gardeningindia #बागवानी

Ask us about your ground, in your language.

Write to BAGIYA in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Hindi or English. The questions we hear most: what is this weed called, which job needs which tool, and when is the right time to clear. Grow: the rake head, for beds you are keeping. Guard: the granules, for ground you want completely clear.

வணக்கம் · నమస్కారం · നമസ്കാരം · नमस्ते

Send us a photo of your ground in a message and ask away.

#களை #కలుపు #കള #growandguard #bagiya

A walking stick is the right height when its handle meets the crease of your wrist.

Stand straight in everyday footwear with the arms hanging loose. The top of the stick should be level with the wrist crease, so the elbow bends slightly when you hold it. Too long pushes the shoulder up; too short makes you stoop.

Hold it in the hand opposite the side that needs support. If you are unsure, ask the shop to help you adjust it.

Worth checking the next time you visit your parents.

#familycare #wellnessathome #indianparents #dailyuse

On a low kitchen counter, the back rounds over the chakla with every roti.

Put a thick flat board or tray under the chakla to bring the work up to you. Stand close with the feet hip-width apart, and roll with the wrists straight and the elbows close to the body. Stop if anything hurts.

What is your own kitchen comfort habit? Let us know below.

#wellnessathome #jointcare #familycare #dailyuse

Many early writers leave no gap between words, so a whole line reads like one long word.

A simple fix used in many classrooms: after each word, lay the index finger of the other hand on the line and start the next word after it. It gives a steady gap every time. Once the gap is a habit, the finger stays home.

Show your child the trick on the next practice page.

#handwritingpractice #kidslearning #studyathome #shribazaar

Many Indian schools moved children from pencil to pen partway through primary school.

For a lot of us, that first day with ink felt like a promotion: a new pen, a careful first line, and ink on the fingers by lunch.

Fountain pen, ball pen, gel pen, or still on pencil? Which one was yours? We would love to hear it.

#indianparents #kidslearning #handwritingpractice #familycare

Writing on a wall sheet tips the wrist back without anyone having to say a word.

Tape a large sheet of paper to a wall or a door at your child's chest height. An upright surface sets the wrist slightly back and brings the elbow and shoulder into every stroke. It is a common play-based warm-up before table writing.

Start with big circles, loops and zigzags, then move to the notebook at the table.

Try it this week with one big sheet and a crayon.

#handwritingpractice #kidslearning #studyathome #indianparents

Tearing paper into small strips is a pinch workout for the thumb and fingertips.

Four everyday games that build a writing hand, no notebook needed: tearing paper, clipping pegs onto a box, rolling tiny dough balls, and dropping rajma into a bottle one at a time.

Keep small items for supervised play only, and away from little mouths.

Swipe through, then save this post for a rainy afternoon.

#kidslearning #handwritingpractice #madeforindia #shribazaar

The lower back muscles run in two long bands, one on either side of the spine.

That is where our soothing massage gel goes: a little on flat palms, then slow circles on the muscles to the left and right of the spine, working outward. Not on the spine itself and not on broken skin. Wash your hands after.

Cooling, fast-absorbing and dries without leaving the skin sticky. Pack of 2 jars, for external use only.

Link in bio to see the gel.

#jointcare #shribazaar #madeforindia #indianparents

Most families have a comfort ritual for tired knees that was handed down from a grandmother.

For some it was mustard oil warmed in a spoon. For others, a warm cloth, a hot-water bottle, or a grandchild sent to press her legs after dinner.

What did your grandmother reach for? Tell us in the comments.

#familycare #indianparents #wellnessathome #jointcare

Pencil leads are graded: an HB is harder than a 2B, so it needs more pressure for a dark line.

A softer 2B leaves the same dark line with a lighter touch. For a child who grips hard and presses through the page, it is an easy thing to try alongside regular practice.

Something to pick up on the next stationery shop visit.

#studyathome #kidslearning #dailyuse #madeforindia

A four-book practice set does not have to start with letters. Drawing can come first.

A suggested order for our Magic Practice Copybook set: the drawing book for strokes and shapes, then numbers, then letters, then maths. Or simply let your child choose the book each day. The pages are grooved, and the set comes with 10 refills. It is a practice aid, used at your child's own pace.

A phone left charging across the room means getting out of bed every time it rings.

Five small changes for a parent's room: lamp, water and phone within reach of the bed. A plastic stool and a rubber mat in the bathroom. Daily things between waist and shoulder height in the kitchen. Loose rugs put away and wires run along the wall.

Save this post for your next visit home.

#wellnessathome #dailyuse #familycare #jointcare

In loose slip-on chappals, the toes grip down with every step just to keep them on.

A back strap or a closed heel holds the chappal to the foot instead, so it moves with each step. It feels steadier on stairs and on wet bathroom floors.

A small change for parents. Worth a look at the chappals by the door this week.

#familycare #wellnessathome #dailyuse #madeforindia

The muscle across the top of the shoulder runs from the skull's base to the shoulder tip.

So work the same way: a little of our Soothing Massage Gel on the fingertips, start at the base of the skull, move slowly down the back of the neck, then along the top of each shoulder to its tip. Light pressure, and never on the front of the throat.

Cooling, fast-absorbing and dries without leaving the skin sticky. Pack of 2 jars, for external use only.

You can find the gel through the link in our bio.

#jointcare #shribazaar #wellnessathome #indianparents

Touching each fingertip to the thumb, one by one, is a classic warm-up before writing.

Add two more and you have thirty seconds of finger warm-ups: open and close both hands slowly, fingertip to thumb and back again, then press the palms together gently and let go.

A calm way to start the practice page. Try it before tonight's homework.

#studyathome #handwritingpractice #kidslearning #madeforindia

Night trips to the bathroom happen half-awake, which is when footing is least sure.

A small plug-in night light along the path from the bed to the bathroom, and one inside, means nobody has to hunt for a switch in the dark.

Good night from all of us at Shri Bazaar.

#familycare #wellnessathome #dailyuse #shribazaar

Walk backwards down the bed while you weed.

Face the plants, weed toward you and step back as you go. That way your feet only ever land on ground you have not worked yet, and you never tread on the soil you have just loosened. Walk in along the unworked side first, then weed your way back out: your own footprints get raked out as you go.

निराई करते हुए पीछे की ओर चलिए।

Which way do you move while weeding: forward or backward? We would like to know how you do it.

#बागवानी #kitchengarden #weeding #bagiya

Cut a weed and it often comes back with two shoots.

The growing tip at the top of a stem holds back the buds lower down. Take the top off with a sickle or a blade and those buds wake up, so the weed branches and bushes out. The root below is exactly where it was, which is why a cut patch looks thicker a little later.

களையை வெட்டினால், இரண்டு தளிர்களாக மீண்டும் வளரும்.

For ground you want completely clear, the job is at the root. Granules clear whatever they reach, so never use them on lawns, beds or crops you are keeping; wear gloves and keep away from children, pets and plants you want. Do you cut or pull on your ground?

#களை #tamilnadu #weedcontrol #growandguard

Getting a bed ready to sow, one pass at a time.

Pass 1: lift the weeds out, setting the teeth just behind each one and drawing the stroke toward you. Pass 2: loosen only the top few centimetres with short strokes across the bed. Pass 3: turn the head over and tap the clods with the back of the teeth until they crumble. Pass 4: level the surface and firm it once, lightly. Then sow.

बुवाई से पहले क्यारी, एक-एक करके तैयार करें।

Our 5-teeth rake head does all four passes; it is a head only and fits a standard wooden pole. Save this post for your next sowing. Which pass takes you longest?

#gardeningindia #terracegarden #gardeningtools #बागवानी #growandguard

On sloping ground, clear from the top down.

Weeds pile up at the low edge of a sloping plot, so that is where most people start. But the few weeds at the top set seed, and every rain carries that seed downhill. Clear the low edge first and it simply fills up again. Start at the top, then the middle, then the bottom.

వాలు నేలలో పై నుంచి కిందికి శుభ్రం చేయండి.

Where is yours thickest: 1 the top, 2 the middle or 3 the low edge? Tell us in the comments. Granules clear whatever they reach: never on lawns, beds or crops you are keeping. Wear gloves; keep away from children, pets and plants you want. Link in bio.

The weeding isn't finished until the soil is covered.

Once a bed is weeded and loosened, the soil is bare. In hot sun the top dries into a hard crust, and new weed seed carried by wind or water lands straight on it. A thin layer of dry leaves or straw laid between the plants keeps the surface shaded and moist, and keeps the soil loose for the next time you weed.

Keep the layer thin, and leave a small gap around each stem.

What do you cover your beds with: 1 dry leaves, 2 straw, 3 nothing yet? Tell us in the comments.

हिंदी: निराई के बाद मिट्टी ढक दें, सूखी पत्तियों या पुआल की पतली परत से।

#terracegarden #weeding #gardeningindia #growandguard

The weed with a parachute.

Coat buttons (Tridax) has a small daisy-like flower: cream rays around a yellow centre, on a long bare stalk above toothed leaves. Each of its small seeds carries a feathery tuft, so the wind picks them up and carries them off. That is why it is so often one of the first weeds to appear on ground that has just been cleared or dug: bare soil, and nothing there yet to shade it out.

காற்றில் பறந்து வரும் களை: வெட்டுக்காயப் பூண்டு.

Is it on your ground? What do you call it? Tell us in the comments.

#களை #tamilnadu #weeds #bagiya

Along a wall, a strip, not a scatter.

Weeds at a boundary wall do not spread across the whole plot: they grow in a narrow line right at the base, where soil and moisture collect against the wall. So that is where the granules go, in a narrow strip along that line and nowhere else, stopping well short of any pot, bed or plant you want to keep.

Sprinkle onto the soil, water lightly, leave it. No spray, no mixing. The granules clear whatever they reach, so never use them on lawns, beds or crops you are keeping. Wear gloves; keep away from children, pets and plants you want.

గోడ వెంట సన్నని వరుసగా వేయండి, అంతటా చల్లకండి.

Before you clear a patch, ask four questions.

1. Is anything here you want to keep? Then work around it by hand or with a rake; granules never go near it.
2. Is it flowering or seeding? Take the heads off first and bag them, so the seed does not drop while you work.
3. Does it spread by runners or tubers, like doob or nutgrass? Pulling snaps them and leaves pieces behind that grow again.
4. Is it a wall base, path or corner you want completely bare? That is where granules belong: sprinkle, water lightly, leave it.

ഒരു സ്ഥലം വൃത്തിയാക്കും മുമ്പ്, ഈ നാല് ചോദ്യങ്ങൾ ചോദിക്കൂ.

Granules clear whatever they reach. Wear gloves; keep away from children, pets and plants you want. Save this post.

#കള #kerala #களை #gardeningindia #bagiya

Dig deep to weed, and you plant the next batch.

Every bed holds a bank of weed seeds, buried at all depths. Most of them only sprout from the top few centimetres, where there is light. Dig a spade deep to get the weeds out and you turn buried seeds up to the surface, where they wake up. A shallow stroke through the top layer lifts the weeds that are growing and leaves the buried seeds where they are, waiting in the dark.

That shallow stroke is what our 5-teeth rake head is for. It is a head only: handle not included; fits a standard wooden pole.

जितना गहरा खोदेंगे, उतने नए खरपतवार।

How deep do you go when you weed: 1 just the top, 2 a hand deep, 3 a spade deep? Tell us in the comments. 🌱

#बागवानी #kitchengarden #weeding #terracegarden #growandguard

The peepal on your wall was planted by a bird.

Birds eat peepal and banyan figs, then sit on parapets, terrace edges, wall tops and wires. The seeds pass through and drop right there, into a joint or crack in the wall. That is why a peepal seedling can appear on a wall with no tree anywhere nearby.

The roots follow the crack into the wall, and as they thicken they can widen it. So pull the seedling out while it is still small, roots and all, instead of cutting off the top.

Is there one on your wall or terrace right now? Tell us where.

മലയാളം: ചുമരിലെ അരയാൽ നട്ടത് ഒരു പക്ഷിയാണ്. ചെറുതായിരിക്കുമ്പോൾ തന്നെ വേരോടെ പിഴുതു മാറ്റുക.

#kerala #കള #walls #bagiya

Dig in. Pull back. Shake off.

Weeds lift out most easily from soil that is damp but not sticky. Squeeze a handful of bed soil: if it crumbles, weed now; if it smears and sticks, wait a day; if it is dust or baked hard, water the evening before.

Then the stroke, with the BAGIYA 5-Teeth Weeding Rake Head:
1. Set the teeth into the soil just behind the weed.
2. Pull the head toward you.
3. Shake the soil off the roots, back onto the bed.

Five pointed carbon-steel teeth, a 20 cm wide head. Head only: the handle is not included, and it fits a standard wooden pole. Made for weeds between the plants you are keeping.

Save this post for your next weeding day. 🌱

Devanagari letters hang from a top line, the shirorekha. English letters sit on one.

A child learning both scripts switches direction every time they change books.

Before practice, point to the line that is home: the top line for Hindi, the bottom line for English.

Which script came first at your home? Tell us in the comments.

#handwritingpractice #kidslearning #indianparents #studyathome

A pot held at arm's length loads the back far more than the same pot held close.

Distance works like a lever: the further the weight sits from the body, the harder the back and shoulders work to hold it.

Carry a full kadhai or pressure cooker with both hands, elbows bent and the pot close to the waist. Where you can, slide it along the counter instead of lifting.

Keep this in mind for the next heavy pot.

#wellnessathome #familycare #dailyuse #madeforindia

The groove guides the pen; a plain page shows what the hand remembers.

One way to use the Magic Practice Copybook: trace a letter in the grooved page a few times, then write it once on plain paper or a slate beside the book.

Golfers pick a ball out of the hole by lifting one leg behind them as a counterweight.

The same move works at home for light things like a pen, a key or a spoon. Hold a chair back or the counter with one hand, bend forward from the hips and let one leg lift straight out behind you as you reach down. The leg balances the reach, so the lower back is not doing all the work.

Keep the standing knee soft, go slowly, and stop if anything hurts.
